facts.claim: Monitum (section 46(1)): an authorised celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say, in the presence of the parties and witnesses, the words: 'I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law. Before you are joined in marriage in my presence and in the presence of these witnesses, I am to remind you of the solemn and binding nature of the relationship into which you are now about to enter. Marriage, according to law in Australia, is the union of 2 people to the exclusion of all others, voluntarily entered into for life.' or words to that effect.
facts.publisher: Federal Register of Legislation, Marriage Act 1961 (compilation 9 July 2024)
facts.use_note: Original note: quoted from the Act text as extracted; 'who is not a minister of religion' scope is medium, the words are high. Quote exactly. Deciding authority on the day: the celebrant.

facts.claim: Vows (section 45(2)): where a marriage is solemnised by or in the presence of an authorised celebrant who is not a minister of religion, each party must say to the other, in the presence of the celebrant and the witnesses: 'I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)' or words to that effect. Under section 45(1), a minister of religion may use the form or ceremony recognised by their religious body. A certificate of marriage prepared and signed under section 50 is conclusive evidence the marriage was solemnised in accordance with section 45.
facts.publisher: Federal Register of Legislation, Marriage Act 1961 (compilation 9 July 2024)
facts.use_note: Original note: vow words read verbatim (high); s 45(1) religious-form rule and the 'not a minister of religion' scope medium. Give the vow words, say 'or words to that effect', and say religious ceremonies follow their own rites. Deciding authority: the celebrant.

facts.claim: Vows (section 45(2)): where the celebrant is not a minister of religion, each party says to the other, in the presence of the celebrant and the witnesses, the prescribed words or words to that effect. The monitum (s 46) is also said 'in the presence of these witnesses'.
facts.publisher: Federal Register of Legislation, Marriage Act 1961 (compilation 9 July 2024)
facts.use_note: Original note: shows why witnesses must be present for the legal words. AGD Guidelines (2018) allow 'these witnesses' in the monitum to become 'everyone here' but not 'family and friends' (not used in copy).

facts.claim: AGD Guidelines 11.6 and 11.7: celebrants may conduct commitment ceremonies, which are not marriages and must not purport to be one. The celebrant must not prepare or submit any paperwork (such as the NOIM and declarations as to conjugal status). Witnesses are not required for a commitment ceremony. A certificate of marriage, or any certificate referring to the Marriage Act, must not be prepared, and celebrants should avoid the words 'wedding' or 'marriage'. The same applies to renewal of vows ceremonies.
facts.publisher: Attorney-General's Department, Guidelines on the Marriage Act 1961 for authorised celebrants (version 4.0, July 2018)
facts.use_note: Medium because the September 2021 edition was not opened (witnesses pack N-002). Supports: vow renewals and commitment ceremonies are not marriages, so no legal words, NOIM, certificate or witnesses.

facts.claim: The Attorney-General's Department says overseas marriages cannot be performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant or registered in Australia, and an overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid in the overseas country and would have been valid here. Legal basis: Marriage Act 1961, Part VA.
facts.use_note: A ceremony abroad led by an Australian celebrant is symbolic unless the local legal process is also followed.

facts.claim: Legal at home, celebration abroad: Australia has no marriage licence; the formal step is giving a Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Since 12 June 2024 the NOIM can be witnessed remotely by audio-visual link, and a couple outside Australia can complete it with an authorised witness overseas (such as an Australian consular officer or a notary public, not a celebrant).
facts.use_note: Present as an option, not advice: legal ceremony in Australia, symbolic ceremony abroad.

legal.summary: Marriage Act 1961 s 45(2) vow words (or words to that effect), said before the celebrant and witnesses; religious ministers may use their own rites (s 45(1)). Your celebrant confirms the wording on the day.
Monitum (s 46(1)) said by the celebrant. Your celebrant confirms the wording on the day.
Commitment and vow renewal ceremonies are not marriages: no NOIM, no certificate, witnesses not required. AGD Guidelines (2018 edition).
An Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas. Confirmed by AGD.
NOIM given at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Confirmed by AGD and your celebrant.
